newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-EUROPE V AFRICA MATCH KICKS OFF YEAR AGAINST RACISM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EUROPE V AFRICA MATCH KICKS OFF YEAR AGAINST RACISM.

text.p: An All-Star European team will play an All-Star African team for the first time ever as part of an iniative to build better soccer ties between the two continents, the European and African ruling soccer bodies announced jointly on Monday.
The game will take place in Lisbon on Wednesday, January 29 with all proceeds being used to finance football projects in Africa.

It is UEFA's first contribution to the European Community's "European Year Against Racism" campaign, and UEFA said on Monday that the match "will mark a new era in the relationship between the African Football Confederation (CAF) and UEFA."

There will also be a meeting of soccer chiefs from the two continents in Lisbon three days after the match and the Portuguese capital will also stage the Meridian Cup, an under-17 tournament involving France, Greece, Portugal, Spain, Ghana, Guinea, Ivory Coast and Nigeria, between January 31 and February 9.
UEFA's involvement in the project is a direct result of the European Commission asking president Lennart Johansson for UEFA's involvement.

Two weeks ago Johansson did not deny making some racist comments of his own after attending a meeting in South Africa, but said the remarks were meant as a joke which he admitted were stupid and had backfired.
